title: phanera integrifolia subsp. cumingiana
intro: Phanera integrifolia subsp. cumingiana, commonly known as the Mountain Madder or Cuming's rattan, is a species of flowering plant in the family Apocynaceae. It is traditionally used in various cultures for its medicinal properties, particularly in treating fever, cough, and respiratory issues, due to its health benefits in boosting the immune system and reducing inflammation. The therapeutic actions of Phanera integrifolia subsp. cumingiana include its antimicrobial, anti-inflammatory, and antioxidant properties, which contribute to its potential in treating various health conditions. The bioactive constituents of the plant include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and alkaloids, which are responsible for its therapeutic effects and are being studied for their potential in developing new medications.
